sb_prompt: DISCUSS RECENT SOCIAL CHANGES.  HOW IS LIFE IN AMERICA DIFFERENT TODAY COMPARED TO LIVING TEN YEARS AGO?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantB: You got through? That was a weird call I got five minutes ago, thought you were a scam.
ParticipantA: Hey, don't worry about it. Just glad to hear from a human. So, how's the farming stuff treating you these days?
ParticipantB: Honestly? It's a rollercoaster. Weather is just getting more insane. We had a freeze in March, then a heatwave in April, and now the rains are just not coming.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I've seen that everywhere. Last year my big tank froze solid in the winter, took me three days to thaw out the pipes. It was a nightmare.
ParticipantB: Oh man, that sucks. My buddy Ray lost half his crop last fall because of the frost. He's still mad about it, says he's never seen anything like it.
ParticipantA: That's tough for him. You know, I've been doing plumbing for ten years now, and honestly, the job is changing pretty fast.
ParticipantB: Really? How's that?
ParticipantA: Well, the manual stuff is still there, but more and more people just want the smart stuff. Like, I can't fix everything myself anymore. I have to rely on these new sensors and apps.
ParticipantB: That makes sense. Technology is pushing into everything, even down here in the fields. We got these new automated irrigation systems last year.
ParticipantA: Yeah, but sometimes it feels like you lose the human element. Like, when something breaks, you're just waiting for the robot to tell you what to do.
ParticipantB: I get that. But for us, the land is still the boss. The machines help, but the ground decides if we eat or starve.
ParticipantA: True. Though, I will say, the younger guys like you seem more open to trying new things than I am. I'm kinda stuck in my ways sometimes.
ParticipantB: Haha, fair enough. I guess I've got to keep up, or else the farm goes up in smoke. Do you feel the same about society in general, or just work?
ParticipantA: Both, really. It feels like people are more connected online but more lonely in real life. My daughter spends hours on her phone, barely talks to me.
ParticipantB: That happens everywhere. My wife and I tried to ban phones at dinner last Christmas, and honestly? It was weird at first, but we're glad we did.
ParticipantA: Good for you. That's a good step. I'm still working on that part of it. Sometimes I just want to talk, not scroll.
ParticipantB: Yeah, me too. It's nice to just hear a voice without the screen in between.
ParticipantA: Exactly. Anyway, I think that's enough to cover for now. Thanks for chatting.
ParticipantB: No problem. Talk soon.
